newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday on the back of a powerful technical rebound on the stock markets, which pushed up demand on the repo market, traders said.
The most active three-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 6.80 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover rose slightly to 3.43 million lots from 3.21 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The stock markets rose on Wednesday after Beijing said there was no big change of the health of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping. Concerns over his health made the markets plunge on Tuesday.
"The recovery of the stock markets pushed up demand for money on the repo market," said one trader. "That in turn pushed up the repo rates, especially the early-maturing contracts."
Traders said they expected the rates to continue to rise in the next few days if there was no further negative news concerning the health of Deng.
"There are a number of new domestic share listings in the next few days, which will boost demand on the repo market and help the rates to rise," said a second trader.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on improved sentiment after Deng health worries weakened.
The market lost heavily on Tuesday on the Deng rumours.

On Wednesday, the most active three-year T-note that matures in Oct 1999 rose to 104.10 yuan from 103.50 yuan on Tuesday. The new two-year note, which was listed on Tuesday and will mature in January 1999, rose to 82.64 yuan from 82.30 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 2.11 million lots from 1.53 million on Tuesday.

The Finance Minstry announced on Tuesday that it would issue 123 billion yuan worth of two-, three- and five-year bonds from March 1 to October 20. Traders said the news had little impact on the market. - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
